Game Design & Production Spec · Hybrid PWA + Printable Deck

Yes, And Away! turns any car ride or airport gate into a family improv stage

A voice-first, zero-prop travel game built around classic improv warm-ups and 3-card scene starters—engineered for hands-free mobile play on the road and 1-to-1 printable poker cards at the table.

One unified card engine powers both the mobile app and the printed deck

Most family travel games fail for one of two reasons: trivia and board games require eyes on a board or tiny text (impossible for a driver and rough on motion-sick kids), while pure verbal games like 20 Questions or I Spy lose steam after 15 minutes. Meanwhile, classic improv warm-ups and scene games—like Yes, And Story, Questions Only, and Park Bench—require zero physical space and scale effortlessly from age 5 to grandparent.

The core invention: every prompt in Yes, And Away! lives in a single JSON card schema shared by an offline-first mobile web app (PWA) and a 108-card poker-size print deck. In the car, a passenger or the app's voice reader deals prompts aloud; at a café or hotel table, you deal the exact same cards face-up.

108

Standard poker cards (2.5" × 3.5") split across four color-coded suits, giving families over 21,000 unique 3-card scene combinations without expansion packs.

A three-stage trip arc teaches real improv habits without feeling like class

Good improv workshops never throw beginners straight into an open scene; they warm up associative thinking first, establish a grounded Who + Where, and then introduce playful constraints. Yes, And Away! bakes that progression into a 10-to-15 minute loop—or lets families jump straight into whichever stage fits their energy.

Stage 1 · Ignition (Warm-Ups)

1–2 minutes per round. Fast, cooperative brain-starters adapted from KraftyLab and Hoopla Impro: One-Word Story, Five Things Fast, Word Association Dash, and Fortunately / Unfortunately. Zero pressure, everyone speaks.

Stage 2 · Cruising (Scene Starters)

3–5 minutes per scene. Two or three players draw 1 Who + 1 Where + 1 Twist card (or tap Deal Scene in the app). One player is the anchor (e.g., a sleepy park ranger), another enters with a problem, and everyone builds with "Yes, and...".

Stage 3 · Pit Stop (Wildcards)

30–60 second jolts. Any non-playing passenger—or the app's automatic timer—triggers a mid-scene twist: Emotion Switch, Questions Only, Alphabet A–Z, or Half-Life (replay the whole scene in half the time).

Digital app & mobile web spec (PWA)

Build the digital version first as a zero-install Progressive Web App (PWA) using static HTML/CSS/TypeScript (or lightweight React/Preact) with a Service Worker that caches the entire 108-card JSON deck locally. That means it works seamlessly on airplanes, ferries, and mountain highways with zero cell signal and no app-store friction.

  • Co-Pilot Hands-Free Mode: Big tap-anywhere canvas with optional Web Speech API voice readout ("Next scene: A nervous astronaut... at a drive-thru... and you can only speak in questions!") so the driver never looks at a screen.
  • Age-Tier Filtering: One toggle switches between Little Sparks (Ages 5–8), Family Mix (Ages 9+), and Wild Teens & Adults by filtering the `age_min` field in the card JSON.
  • Companion Timer & Bell: Works standalone or alongside physical cards (via a QR code on the printed Rule Card) for 30s, 60s, 90s, and Half-Life countdowns.
  • Pass-the-Phone / Cooperative Scoring: No elimination. After each round, players tap a quick star or laugh badge ("Best Sound Effect", "Saved the Scene") to track family trip highlights without competitive tension.

Starter Pack · 12 Sample Cards

What a real round sounds like in the backseat

Each card uses a 1-second scannable headline, a 10-word prompt, and an optional kid-friendly helper cue so even emerging readers can jump right in.

Warm-Ups (Coral) & Twists (Plum)

  • WU-01 · Five Things Fast: Name 5 things you would NEVER pack in a suitcase—go!
  • WU-04 · Fortunately / Unfortunately: Build a travel disaster story alternating good news and bad news.
  • WU-09 · Sound Ball: Toss an imaginary sound across the car; catch it, repeat it, transform it.
  • TW-02 · Questions Only: Every single line of dialogue must end in a question mark.
  • TW-11 · Emotion Switch: Every 20 seconds, the Co-Pilot calls a new mood: whispering, royal, panicked, sleepy.
  • TW-19 · Alphabet Road: Line 1 starts with A, Line 2 with B, Line 3 with C—keep the scene making sense!

Who (Cobalt) & Where (Teal) Combos

  • WHO-03 · Nervous Astronaut: Trying to look totally cool on their first mission.
  • WHO-12 · Overly Polite Pirate: Apologizes profusely before stealing anything.
  • WHO-21 · Talking Golden Retriever: Desperately wants whatever snack is on the table.
  • WHR-05 · Haunted Drive-Thru: The intercom keeps offering weird upgrades.
  • WHR-14 · Submarine Gift Shop: Everything is slightly damp and overpriced.
  • WHR-27 · Cloud-Nine Airport Gate: Boarding Group 99 is finally called.

Printable physical card & production specification

Designing to standard US Poker dimensions (2.5" × 3.5") from day one means you can print prototype sheets on heavy cardstock at home today and upload the exact same files to a print-on-demand vendor tomorrow without re-laying out a single card.

"The secret to family improv isn't being funny—it's saying Yes, and... to whatever ridiculous thing your eight-year-old just invented."

Four-step build roadmap

  1. Lock the 108-card JSON dataset: Write 24 Warm-Ups, 28 Who, 28 Where, and 28 Twists with age tags (`5+`, `9+`, `13+`) and `quiet_ok` flags.
  2. Ship the offline PWA prototype: Build the single-page mobile web app with tap-to-deal, Web Speech TTS audio mode, and the Half-Life countdown chime.
  3. Add the `/print` 9-up PDF stylesheet: Render the exact same JSON cards onto 12 US Letter pages with crop marks and ink-saving card backs for weekend road-test playtesting.
  4. Export CMYK POD files: Once playtesting trims any awkward prompts, export individual `2.75" × 3.75"` bleed PDFs for a custom printed travel deck and tuck box.
